jobs.title: Data Analyst
jobs.description:
At Zelis, we Get Stuff Done. So, let’s get to it!

A Little About Us

Zelis is modernizing the healthcare financial experience across payers, providers, and healthcare consumers. We serve more than 750 payers, including the top five national health plans, regional health plans, TPAs and millions of healthcare providers and consumers across our platform of solutions. Zelis sees across the system to identify, optimize, and solve problems holistically with technology built by healthcare experts – driving real, measurable results for clients.

At Zelis, AI is woven into the fabric of how we work. Every associate is expected - and empowered - to partner with AI to challenge the status quo, accelerate innovation, and amplify their impact. This is a place for builders with a growth mindset who act with agility, embrace change, and use modern technology to shape smarter solutions, exceptional experiences, and the future of our industry for our clients, customers, and our culture.

A Little About You

You bring a unique blend of personality and professional expertise to your work, inspiring others with your passion and dedication. Your career is a testament to your diverse experiences, community involvement, and the valuable lessons you've learned along the way. You are more than just your resume; you are a reflection of your achievements, the knowledge you've gained, and the personal interests that shape who you are.

Position Overview

The Analyst II, Data Analysis will be responsible for analyzing complex data sets to derive actionable insights and support data-driven decision-making across the organization. This role requires a skilled data analyst with strong analytical abilities, a deep understanding of statistical methods, and the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams. The ideal candidate will have experience in data analysis, excellent problem-solving skills, and a passion for leveraging data to drive business outcomes.

What You’ll Do

Analyze large and complex data sets to identify trends, patterns, and insights.
Develop and implement statistical models and algorithms to solve business problems.
Validate and refine models to ensure accuracy and reliability.
Create clear and compelling data visualizations to communicate findings to stakeholders.
Prepare and present regular reports on data analysis outcomes to senior leadership.
Develop dashboards and other tools to enable self-service data access for business users.
Collect, clean, and preprocess data from various sources to ensure data quality and consistency.
Collaborate with data engineers and IT teams to design and implement data pipelines and workflows.
Ensure data is properly stored, organized, and accessible for analysis.
Work closely with business stakeholders to understand their data needs and provide actionable insights.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including marketing, product, and finance, to support data-driven decision-making.
Provide training and support to team members on data analysis and visualization best practices.
Stay informed about industry trends, emerging technologies, and best practices in data analysis.
Identify opportunities for process improvements and implement innovative solutions.
Attends company training and regional training in area of expertise. Presents own work to members of department.

What You’ll Bring To Zelis

Typically has Bach. +2-3 yrs; Masters +0 yrs
Requires proficiency using AI tools skillfully with an understanding of how to develop/create intelligent prompts and/or agents.
Fluency with data analysis tools (e.g., SQL, Python, R, Excel).
Proficiency with data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI) is a plus.
Healthcare claims editing experience a plus.
Understanding of statistics and data modeling preferred.
Strong communication, analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
Experience presenting findings to senior leadership team
Experience with big data technologies (e.g., Hadoop, Spark) is a plus.
Knowledge of machine learning techniques and algorithms.
Certification in data analysis or related fields.

Please note at this time we are unable to proceed with candidates who require visa sponsorship now or in the future.

Location and Workplace Flexibility

Zelis is headquartered in the U.S., with multiple locations across the country and in Hyderabad, India. Check out our locations to learn more about our offices. All employee work locations are based on the needs of the position and are determined by the Leadership team. In-office work and activities vary based on work and team objectives in accordance with Company policies.

While location expectations vary by role, candidates within approximately 50 miles of a U.S. office are generally preferred to support collaboration when needed. Our hybrid approach is flexible, and in-office presence is guided by team and business needs rather than a fixed weekly schedule.

Base Salary Range

$71,000.00 - $90,250.00

At Zelis we are committed to providing fair and equitable compensation packages. The base salary range allows us to make an offer that considers multiple individualized factors, including experience, education, qualifications, as well as job-related and industry-related knowledge and skills, etc. Base pay is just one part of our Total Rewards package, which may also include discretionary bonus plans, commissions, or other incentives depending on the role.

Zelis’ full-time associates are eligible for a highly competitive benefits package as well, which demonstrates our commitment to our employees’ health, well-being, and financial protection. The US-based benefits include a 401k plan with employer match, flexible paid time off, holidays, parental leaves, life and disability insurance, and health benefits including medical, dental, vision, and prescription drug coverage.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Zelis is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet 100% of the qualifications for the role. We believe in the value of diverse perspectives and experiences and are committed to building an inclusive workplace for all.

Accessibility Support

We are dedicated to ensuring our application process is accessible to all candidates. If you are a qualified individual with a disability or a disabled veteran and require a reasonable accommodation with any part of the application and/or interview process, please email TalentAcquisition@zelis.com.

The Office of Workforce and Community Initiatives (OWCI) is seeking candidates to fill Research/Data Analyst positions located in Cole County based at 3705 MO Blvd 2nd Floor, Jefferson City, MO. Remote or hybrid is not an option.

The essential duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

This position is primarily responsible for transforming OWCI program data into high‑impact visual analytics products that support program leadership, management, and executive‑level decision‑making. Using specialized software such as Tableau, Power BI, MS Office products, and coding languages including Python and SQL, the role creates visually compelling dashboards, interactive reports, and polished briefings that clearly communicate trends, outcomes, and performance indicators, requiring a strong emphasis on data storytelling, intuitive UI/UX design, and the ability to present complex information clearly and accurately. In addition, this position applies data management expertise to support the preparation, refinement, and maintenance of moderate to complex data systems, including analyzing specifications, participating in the installation and testing of data management systems, and supporting system migration into operational environments while ensuring data integrity and security. The role may assist in developing detailed conceptual data models and translating them into design specifications, tuning database applications for optimal performance, and providing technical guidance or leadership to junior staff, while acting with independence and accountability for portions of larger projects.

Gather, blend, and model data from multiple disparate sources to ensure accurate, consistent reporting and a single source of truth for visual analytics products.
Present data in simplified and visually compelling formats that highlight trends, anomalies, KPIs, and program performance through charts, visualizations, and narrative explanations.
Apply UI/UX principles, including effective visual hierarchy, appropriate chart selection, color standards, and accessible dashboard layouts that support both technical and non‑technical users.
Partner with management and executive stakeholders to gather requirements, understand strategic priorities, and convert business questions into clear technical design specifications for visual reporting products.
Review and evaluate legislation for impact on agency operations; prepare visual summaries and analysis to support strategic planning and implementation.
Provide technical guidance on visualization standards, effective dashboard design, and the use of management reporting tools for monitoring program performance.
Perform duties in accordance with supervisor direction and established policies and procedures at all times. Complete assigned tasks in an accurate, timely, professional, and confidential manner.
Assist in reviewing and evaluating the effectiveness and operational management of workforce, medical, and community support programs through visual analytics and performance dashboards.
Demonstrate critical thinking and problem‑solving by crafting clear, concise visual narratives that support decision makers at all levels.

Additional Competencies Drawn From Expanded Data Management Expectations

Knowledge of data modeling and design methodologies.
Ability to think methodically and critically when evaluating data systems and visual products.
Ability to identify, evaluate, and resolve database performance issues.
Ability to organize work, prioritize tasks, and manage multiple assignments simultaneously.

A Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university with a minimum of 24 earned credit hours in one or a combination of the following: Business or Public Administration, Economics, Finance, Industrial Engineering, Engineering Management, or a closely related field; and
, one or more years of professional experience in management analysis, fiscal or financial analysis, operations research, or industrial engineering.

(24 earned graduate credit hours from an accredited college or university in the specified areas may substitute for the required experience.)

(Additional qualifying experience may substitute on a year-for-year basis for deficiencies in the required education.)

Preferred Experience

Experience with data visualization tools such as Tableau, Power BI, or similar platforms; proficiency in Python and SQL; knowledge of data blending and modeling; experience with UI/UX design principles for analytics; previous experience working in or with SkillUP, MWA, A2A, LIHEAP, LIHWAP, CSBG, Jobs League, Food Distribution, VOCA, DVS, JAG, MAGI related data; or other programs overseen by OWCI. jobs.title: Science Data Analyst
jobs.description:
About Lasso Informatics

Research data is wild. It pours in from brain scans, genome sequencing, EEG and eye-tracking, biospecimens and wearables that track sleep and movement, across dozens of sites and years of study. Lasso Informatics ropes it in: our platform pulls it all into one place so researchers around the world can stop fighting with their data and get to discoveries faster. That is where our name comes from. A lasso brings something wild under control, and that is the job. The people who do it are Wranglers, and we are quite choosy about who earns the title. Wranglers expect a lot of themselves, make everyone around them better, and never stop learning. We move fast, we have fun, and we keep the bar high. 

What We Offer

A flexible, hybrid or remote position.
Competitive compensation and benefits.
Work that matters, with scientific and clinical impact you can point to.
Variety that keeps it interesting: you work the whole analytics stack, from study design to insight, so no two projects feel the same.
Room to grow with a mission-driven company at the front of research data management.
A sharp, multidisciplinary team that is good at what it does and good to work with.

Full-Time |
US, Remote or Hybrid (Minneapolis)

US-based: $64,000 - $78,000 USD

Learn more and apply: https://careers.lassoinformatics.info/jobs/science-data-analyst

Want to Be a Wrangler? Here's What We Look For

You hold yourself to a high standard and bring real analytical rigor.
You make the people around you better.
You stay curious and keep learning.
You see a problem and start solving it, without waiting to be asked.
You keep the whole picture in view and notice how a change in one place ripples through the data, the study and the results.
You write clearly, document your methods with precision and explain complex statistical findings to non-technical audiences.
You juggle several priorities at once and work well on a distributed team.
You take data privacy, responsible stewardship and reproducibility seriously.

About the Role 

Read this part first, it saves us both time:
This is a health research role, not business intelligence, financial analytics or management consulting. We are looking for someone who comes from life sciences research and is at home in study design, biostatistics and the messy reality of participant data.

As a Science Data Analyst at Lasso, you sit inside a multidisciplinary research team and help answer real scientific questions. You shape analytical approaches, test them against study design, and turn tangled multi-modal data into findings that hold up. You are comfortable working alongside and communicating with people from every corner of the company, from researchers and software engineers to project managers. 

What You'll Do

 Work directly with researchers to define data requirements, resolve quality issues and support reproducible research workflows.
Conduct statistical analyses in R, Python and other tools, applying biostatistical methods suited to the study design, including mixed-effects models and longitudinal techniques.
Evaluate and contribute to experimental and study design decisions, making sure analyses are valid and that confounds, covariates and sampling are handled properly.
Apply statistical and computational methods for pattern detection, predictive modeling and data quality assessment across multi-modal datasets.
Organize and manage datasets and data dictionaries, run QC checks and conduct preliminary analyses that keep data integrity high.
Design, configure and maintain dashboards for domain-specific workgroups.
Produce clear documentation of your methods, pipelines and findings for scientific and internal audiences.
Maintain project tracking and help build a culture of rigorous, reproducible science.

Qualifications 

Required

A PhD in health or life sciences (for example epidemiology, public health, neuroscience, genetics, genomics, behavioral science or clinical and biomedical sciences). This one is firm: we want a researcher who analyzes data, not a data professional new to health research.
5+ years of full-time experience in data analysis and data science fundamentals (algorithms, data structures, data visualization), preferably in a clinical or research setting.
5+ years of full-time experience in a scientific programming language such as Python, R or Matlab, with hands-on familiarity with related frameworks and libraries (Tidyverse, SciPy, scikit-learn, PyTorch, Polars).
Advanced proficiency in biostatistics, including methods suited to observational (cross-sectional and longitudinal) and experimental research designs.
Demonstrated experience applying experimental design principles: power analysis, randomization, control conditions and bias mitigation.
1+ year working in a Linux environment, using version control (e.g., GitHub) and software virtualization platforms (e.g., Docker).
Proficiency creating visualizations of complex longitudinal datasets.
3+ years working with data privacy regulations (HIPAA, GDPR) and research ethics standards.

Preferred

Background in neuroscience, genomics, clinical research or a related life sciences discipline.
Experience with large-scale, multi-modal research datasets spanning imaging, EEG, eye-tracking, wearables, behavioral, genetic or biosample data.
Familiarity with reproducible research practices including R Markdown, Quarto or equivalent notebook-based workflows.

The Data Analyst plays a key role in enabling data-driven decision making across ResMed's Global Distribution, Logistics & Trade organization. This role supports stakeholders across ResMed's global supply chain network and partners with teams across multiple regions and geographies.

As a member of the Global Supply Chain Performance & Insights team, you will transform complex operational data into actionable insights that improve service, reduce costs, increase efficiency, and support operational excellence across ResMed's global supply chain network.

You will collaborate closely with Distribution, Logistics, Transportation, Trade, Planning, Customer Operations, Finance, and Technology teams to develop dashboards, reporting solutions, performance metrics, and analytical insights that help teams make better business decisions.

This role is ideal for a data professional who enjoys solving business problems, uncovering insights from data, automating manual processes, and working in a highly collaborative global environment.

This is a global role supporting stakeholders across multiple regions and time zones. Candidates must be comfortable collaborating across a globally distributed organization and demonstrate flexibility to participate in occasional early-morning or evening meetings when needed to support regional stakeholders and global business priorities.

What You'll Do

Business Partnership & Insight Generation

Partner with global supply chain stakeholders to understand business needs and translate them into analytical solutions.
Work closely with regional stakeholders to understand operational challenges, business questions and reporting needs and translate them into analytical solutions.
Develop a strong understanding of regional supply chain processes, operating models and business priorities.
Provide data-driven insights and recommendations that help stakeholders make informed operational decisions.
Participate in regional performance reviews and business discussions, providing analytical support and identifying trends, risks and opportunities.
Collaborate effectively with stakeholders across different cultures, geographies and time zones.

Participate in analytics and digital transformation initiatives across the global supply chain organization.
Explore new analytical capabilities, tools and technologies that can improve the way supply chain teams’ access and use information.
Contribute to the team's continued development of self-service, predictive and AI-enabled analytics capabilities.

Bachelor’s degree in data Analytics, Business Analytics, Supply Chain, Engineering, Statistics, Computer Science, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
3+ years of experience in data analytics, business intelligence, operations analytics, supply chain analytics, or a related field.
Strong SQL skills with experience querying and analyzing large datasets.
Experience building dashboards and reporting solutions using Tableau and/or Power BI.
Demonstrated AI literacy, including the ability to effectively use AI-powered tools to enhance data analysis, reporting, problem solving, productivity, and decision making.
Advanced Microsoft Excel skills.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical-thinking abilities.
Ability to translate business questions into analytical solutions and actionable insights.
Excellent communication and presentation skills.
Strong organizational and prioritization abilities with the capability to manage multiple priorities.
Ability to work independently and effectively within a global, cross-functional environment.
Willingness and flexibility to support stakeholders across global time zones, including occasional participation in meetings outside traditional local business hours when required.

What Sets You Apart

Experience within supply chain, logistics, transportation, distribution, manufacturing, healthcare, or medical device environments.
Experience with cloud data platforms such as Snowflake, Databricks, Azure, AWS, or similar technologies.
Experience using Python or other analytics programming languages.
Familiarity with data modeling, ETL processes, and data governance principles.
Experience working with ERP systems such as Oracle.

Experience supporting stakeholders across multiple countries, regions, and time zones.

Business Partnership

Builds strong relationships with stakeholders and understands how analytics can support operational objectives.

Analytical Excellence

Uses structured problem solving, critical thinking, and quantitative analysis to solve business challenges.

Data Storytelling

Communicates analytical findings clearly and effectively to drive understanding and action.

Technical Proficiency

Leverages data, reporting tools, and automation capabilities to create scalable analytical solutions.

Collaboration

Works effectively across functions, regions, and cultures to achieve shared business outcomes.

Continuous Improvement

Actively identifies opportunities to improve processes, reporting, and decision making.

Adaptability

Thrives in a dynamic global environment and effectively supports teams across multiple time zones.

Success in This Role

Successful candidates will:

Become a trusted day-to-day analytics partner for Distribution, Logistics and Supply Chain stakeholders across global regions.
Develop a strong understanding of regional and global supply chain operations while effectively supporting cross-regional and enterprise-wide initiatives.
Deliver accurate, timely and actionable dashboards and analytical insights that improve operational decision making.
Improve visibility into supply chain performance through consistent KPIs, reporting and data visualization.
Identify operational trends, exceptions and improvement opportunities before they become larger business issues.
Reduce manual reporting effort through automation and improved analytical processes.
Improve confidence in data through strong validation, documentation and data-quality practices.
Build effective working relationships across regions and demonstrate flexibility in supporting a globally distributed organization.

Research data is wild. It pours in from brain scans, genome sequencing, EEG and eye-tracking, biospecimens and wearables that track sleep and movement, across dozens of sites and years of study. Lasso Informatics ropes it in: our platform pulls it all into one place so researchers around the world can stop fighting with their data and get to discoveries faster. That is where our name comes from. A lasso brings something wild under control, and that is the job. The people who do it are Wranglers, and we are quite choosy about who earns the title. Wranglers expect a lot of themselves, make everyone around them better, and never stop learning. We move fast, we have fun, and we keep the bar high.

A flexible, hybrid or remote position.
Competitive compensation and benefits.
Work that matters, with scientific and clinical impact you can point to.
Variety that keeps it interesting: you work the whole analytics stack, from study design to insight, so no two projects feel the same.

A sharp, multidisciplinary team that is good at what it does and good to work with.

US, Remote or Hybrid (Minneapolis)

US-based: $64,000 - $78,000 USD

You hold yourself to a high standard and bring real analytical rigor.
You make the people around you better.
You stay curious and keep learning.
You see a problem and start solving it, without waiting to be asked.
You keep the whole picture in view and notice how a change in one place ripples through the data, the study and the results.
You write clearly, document your methods with precision and explain complex statistical findings to non-technical audiences.
You juggle several priorities at once and work well on a distributed team.
You take data privacy, responsible stewardship and reproducibility seriously.

About the Role 

Read this part first, it saves us both time:
This is a health research role, not business intelligence, financial analytics or management consulting. We are looking for someone who comes from life sciences research and is at home in study design, biostatistics and the messy reality of participant data.

As a Science Data Analyst at Lasso, you sit inside a multidisciplinary research team and help answer real scientific questions. You shape analytical approaches, test them against study design, and turn tangled multi-modal data into findings that hold up. You are comfortable working alongside and communicating with people from every corner of the company, from researchers and software engineers to project managers. 

What You'll Do

 Work directly with researchers to define data requirements, resolve quality issues and support reproducible research workflows.

Apply statistical and computational methods for pattern detection, predictive modeling and data quality assessment across multi-modal datasets.
Organize and manage datasets and data dictionaries, run QC checks and conduct preliminary analyses that keep data integrity high.
Design, configure and maintain dashboards for domain-specific workgroups.
Produce clear documentation of your methods, pipelines and findings for scientific and internal audiences.
Maintain project tracking and help build a culture of rigorous, reproducible science.

Qualifications 

Required

A PhD in health or life sciences (for example epidemiology, public health, neuroscience, genetics, genomics, behavioral science or clinical and biomedical sciences). This one is firm: we want a researcher who analyzes data, not a data professional new to health research.
5+ years of full-time experience in data analysis and data science fundamentals (algorithms, data structures, data visualization), preferably in a clinical or research setting.
5+ years of full-time experience in a scientific programming language such as Python, R or Matlab, with hands-on familiarity with related frameworks and libraries (Tidyverse, SciPy, scikit-learn, PyTorch, Polars).
Advanced proficiency in biostatistics, including methods suited to observational (cross-sectional and longitudinal) and experimental research designs.

Proficiency creating visualizations of complex longitudinal datasets.
3+ years working with data privacy regulations (HIPAA, GDPR) and research ethics standards.

Background in neuroscience, genomics, clinical research or a related life sciences discipline.
Experience with large-scale, multi-modal research datasets spanning imaging, EEG, eye-tracking, wearables, behavioral, genetic or biosample data.
Familiarity with reproducible research practices including R Markdown, Quarto or equivalent notebook-based workflows.

Any one or any combination that equals four (4) years/ 48 months of responsible volunteer or professional work experience in coordinating educational and/or community programs or activities

College coursework in any field of study

60 semester hours equals two (2) years (24 months)

Attention to detail and prioritize tasks. Ability to multi-task.
